problem.title: Channel or pair of channels violating p-norm multiplicativity for both some p>1 and some 0<p<1

question.summary: The source asked whether a single channel or channel pair can violate equation (26) simultaneously at some p above 1 and some p below 1. Hastings' fixed finite-dimensional additivity gap at p = 1, combined with continuity of the minimum output Renyi entropy in p, supplies such a pair.
question.importance: All known constructions were non-uniform in p, with the dimension blowing up as p approaches 1 and structurally different Kraus operators above and below one, and a negative answer would have forced a one-sided approach to p = 1 and reopened a route to the additivity conjecture there.

problem.titleMarkdown: Channel(s) violating $p$-norm multiplicativity for both $p_1>1$ and $0<p_2<1$

targetClauses.label: Simultaneous multiplicativity violation above and below p = 1
targetClauses.text: The archived statement asks whether there exists a quantum channel, or a pair of channels on finite-dimensional matrix algebras, and values p1 > 1 and 0 < p2 < 1 such that the multiplicativity equality (26) fails at both.
targetClauses.resolutionCriteria: A single channel or channel pair violating the identity on both sides of p = 1, or a proof that violation is always one-sided.

claims.title: Hastings gap plus continuity in p gives a two-sided violation
claims.text: Hastings produced a fixed finite-dimensional channel pair with a strict additivity gap at p = 1, and for fixed finite-dimensional channels the minimum output Renyi entropy is continuous in p at 1 because the state Renyi entropy is jointly continuous in state and order and the input-state set is compact. The strict gap therefore persists on an interval around one, and choosing one order on each side of one gives the single pair requested; Leung, Lovitz and Wu independently make this implication explicit and prove nonadditivity for every p > 3/4.

evidence.sourceLocator: Main result: fixed finite-dimensional channel pair with a strict additivity gap at p = 1
evidence.label: Nature Physics

evidence.sourceLocator: Explicit continuity implication and nonadditivity for every p > 3/4
evidence.label: arXiv:2607.15210

decisions.rationale: Hastings' peer-reviewed finite-dimensional gap at p = 1, combined with continuity of the minimum output Renyi entropy in p, yields a channel pair violating equation (26) on both sides of one, which is exactly what the archived statement asks for. The corroborating Leung-Lovitz-Wu manuscript was an unrefereed first version at the audit cutoff; the resolution does not depend on it.

cautions.label: Scope
cautions.text: The solved label follows the source's explicit equation (26) for minimum output standard Renyi entropy; the continuity argument does not answer the different question of conventional maximal-output p-quasinorm multiplicativity for p < 1.
